title: Minimum Number of Coins for Fruits II
summary: Given an array prices representing the cost of each fruit, where purchasing the i-th fruit allows you to get the next i fruits free, determine the minimum coins required to acquire all the fruits, considering you can purchase any fruit to get future fruits free.
statement: Given an array prices representing the cost of each fruit, where purchasing the i-th fruit allows you to get the next i fruits free, determine the minimum coins required to acquire all the fruits, considering you can purchase any fruit to get future fruits free.
constraints: Buying fruit i (one-indexed) grants the next i fruits for free, though a free fruit may still be bought to extend benefits.
Return the minimum coins needed to acquire every fruit.
hints: After buying index i, the next paid fruit may be any position through 2i+2 in zero-based indexing.
Compute minimum remaining cost backward over those reachable next purchase positions.
dp[i]=price[i]+min(dp[j]) for j in i+1..2i+2, with out-of-range dp zero.
Choosing j also acquires all intervening fruits for free; every valid purchasing plan has exactly one such next paid position.

tests.explanation: Buy the first fruit for three and the second for one to cover all fruits, totaling four.
Strategic purchases of free fruits extend coverage at minimum total cost.
